name: MCP2551
description: High-speed CAN transceiver providing the physical-layer interface between a CAN protocol controller (such as the MCP2515 or an MCU's on-chip CAN) and the differential two-wire bus. It has short-circuit protection on the bus lines (a different, more limited guarantee than a genuinely fault-tolerant ISO 11898-3 transceiver, which keeps communicating on a broken/shorted wire), supports up to 1 Mbit/s and at least 112 nodes, and offers a slope-control mode via the Rs pin to reduce EMI on slower buses. A 5 V part: it converts the controller's logic-level TXD/RXD to the CANH/CANL differential pair.

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: transmit data input from the CAN controller

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: receive data output to the CAN controller

pins.name: Rs
pins.description: slope/mode select: resistor to ground sets slew rate; high = standby mode

typical_application: Physical-layer driver between a CAN controller (MCP2515 or MCU CAN core) and the differential bus; pairs with the MCP2515 on most CAN shields.
gotchas: a 5 V part (4.5-5.5 V); if your controller/MCU runs at 3.3 V, TXD/RXD logic levels must be reconciled - many 3.3 V designs use the 3.3 V SN65HVD230 instead
Rs (pin 8) sets the mode: tie to ground for high-speed, add a resistor to ground for slope control (lower EMI), pull high for standby - leaving it floating misbehaves
CANH/CANL need 120 ohm termination at both ends of the bus, not at every node
it is a transceiver only, no protocol logic; it must be driven by a CAN controller
newer designs often prefer the TJA1050/TJA1051 or SN65HVD230; the MCP2551 has a higher minimum current draw
